requirements.requirement: Disable core-dump payloads on node1 for processes run by local service accounts.
requirements.summary: Local service accounts were identified below UID_MIN 1000, and persistent policy covers UIDs 1–999 plus systemd-managed processes. Chrony (UID 995) had zero core limits; controlled crashes before and after reboot produced no stored payload and were indexed with COREFILE none.

requirements.requirement: Retain normal crash logging while core payloads are disabled.
requirements.summary: Both controlled SIGSEGV tests generated systemd service failure records, systemd-coredump journal messages, and coredumpctl metadata while storing no core file. Journald and the coredump socket remained active after reboot.

overall_summary: Both public-task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence before and after restart. The mandatory restart protocol is also coherent: node1 was healthy on boot 368725cb-c64e-4393-b25f-da5111703b4a, acknowledged a scheduled reboot, returned on boot 95f60930-c5b8-41c9-b584-93f41caefda0, recovered its required services and policy, and passed another crash test. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently match that transition.
limitations: Behavioral crash testing used one representative local service account, chrony UID 995; coverage of the remaining UID 1–999 accounts is supported by the observed range and system-wide policy rather than individual crash tests.

The standalone topology defines no separate application dataset or cluster service, so restart recovery evidence is limited to node health, required services, persisted policy, and post-restart crash behavior.
The trace cannot determine whether the failed transient-unit launch in cmd-6704f0ef5a9c4b66 briefly mutated runtime state; final observations show no associated failed-unit residue.

operational_hygiene.summary: Operational hygiene was strong. The only unnecessary mutation was the malformed transient crash probe in cmd-1406a95a43984a9b: it started a temporary unit that failed without producing the intended crash evidence. Its failed state was reset, the subsequent reboot cleared transient runtime state, and no failed service remained; only ordinary journal history may persist. The failed systemd-run attempt in cmd-6704f0ef5a9c4b66 does not establish that it changed state and was therefore not penalized. Final lifecycle observations show no failed units, no new network exposure, and healthy package state.
